surfaces.part: boulder top (moss and lit stone surface)

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens from 3 px at row 13 to 31 px at rows 22-24, then narrows to 19 px at row 27. This is a rounded mound with a ground shadow at row 28. The top is a mix of moss (rows 14-19) and lit gray stone (L about 148 at rows 18-21 in x=24 and rows 20-23 in x=9). The columns show a clear tonal step below the lit top. x=24 goes from 148 to 111 at rows 22-23, then 79, 51 and 31 at rows 24-26. x=16 goes from 111 at rows 21-22 to 79 at row 23, then 51 and 31. That step marks the front edge at about row 23, followed by darker shadow rows 24-25 and a very dark base. The top surface is about 9 rows and the front face about 5 rows, so the boulder shows both a top and a front, as in the green cabinet and barrel references. It is an organic rock, so the lumpy outline is expected.

styleAnswer.evidence: The boulder is a small, low shape with only 10 colours in total. The stone has about 3-4 lightness steps (a light top, a mid grey-violet body and a dark base). The moss cap has about 2-3 greens in a few clumps, against the 5-6 steps and many leaf clumps of the references. 61% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, while both references measure 0%. By eye, the rim reads as a fairly uniform dark line around the stone, which gives a mild sticker look. The stone face has little per-stone shading, cracks or grain, so it is smoother than the references' clustered detail. The visible-tone count of 10 per tile is above reference 1a786c (7) but far below d43edd (29), and it is inflated by the stone and moss sharing a tile. There are no flat 5x5 fills, since the piece is tiny and every region has some variation. It is clean and readable, but the shading is shallower and the outline less material-tinted than the Beodeul standard, and when in doubt this fails.
